title: I want to message them again
blurb: For the gap between sending something and hearing back, when the waiting has its own gravity.
entry_signals: I want to know where I stand

steps.ask: How strong is the pull right now, one to ten?

steps.title: Wait out the peak
steps.say:
At this level the message isn't really asking a question — it's trying to end a feeling, and it will read that way at the other end no matter how carefully it's worded.

The pull does drop. Not because you talked yourself out of it, but because the state passes. Give it an hour and put the need somewhere else in the meantime — a person, a walk, anything that isn't this thread.

steps.ask: Is there a practical reason you need an answer — a plan, a decision, something with a deadline?
steps.help: Sometimes the message is just admin, and the flow shouldn't talk you out of a normal thing.

options.label: Partly, but that's not really why
No — I want to know we're okay

steps.title: Then send it
steps.say:
Send the practical message, keep it to the practical thing, and don't attach the other question to it.

A logistics message carrying a hidden bid for reassurance tends to get a logistics reply, which then hurts more than no reply would have.

steps.ask: What have you already sent, and when?
steps.help: Just the record. How many, and how long since the last one.

steps.ask: What are you hoping the reply does?
cites: I Can Only Feel Better Through Someone Else

options.label: Tells me we're fine so I can stop feeling like this
options.names: I Can Only Feel Better Through Someone Else
cites: I Can Only Feel Better Through Someone Else

options.label: Gives me information I don't have
Makes them realise how this is landing on me

steps.ask_a: What do you actually know about the silence?
steps.help_a: Facts only. When they last replied, what you know about their week.
steps.ask_b: And what have you concluded from it?
steps.help_b: The story that's been running. Write it as baldly as it actually sounds.

steps.say: Worth knowing about the searching: looking hard for evidence that something is wrong tends to find some, because a search that specific always does. And what started as a fear comes back feeling like knowledge — which raises the pull to check again.

steps.ask: If you were going to say the real thing, what would it be?
steps.help: Not the casual message. The actual one — something like: I've noticed I get worried when it goes quiet, and I'd rather tell you than keep guessing. It's more exposing, and it's the only version that can get a real answer.

steps.ask: And what's the part of this that doesn't depend on them replying at all?
steps.help: How long you're willing to wait before you ask directly. What you'll do with the evening. The bit that stays yours.

steps.say: Two things to leave with: the honest sentence, and the part that doesn't need them. Sending the first is optional. The second one is available tonight either way.
